runs.failure_point: It added a sale-side buyer matter as qualifying on a broad reading of the request, after reading only its asset-purchase agreement and engagement letter.

first_error.why: It had read only the sale-side matter's asset-purchase agreement and engagement letter (evidence seen at [56]-[80]), which show a buyer in a sale under a court-authorised financing, yet the answer adds it as a DIP-related matter on a broad reading.
first_error.critic_note: (specific flag) The write review asked it to decide whether the peripheral matter had actual DIP involvement and move it to the exclusions if not; the check stage re-read its agreement and engagement letter and kept it, and the last check review endorsed keeping it labelled separately.

runs.failure_point: It counted a sale-side buyer matter among the qualifying matters because the buyer coordinated with the seller's financing facility.

first_error.why: The answer counts the sale-side matter as a matter with actual DIP involvement because the buyer coordinated with the seller's DIP facility, from its engagement letter, diligence memo and a draft closing checklist (evidence seen at [48]-[75]).
first_error.critic_note: (specific flag) The screening review said the buyer classification of that matter rested on thin evidence; it read the draft checklist and asset-purchase agreement and kept the matter, and both check reviews said not to change the matter set.

divergence: Mixed (T1 passes; T0, T2 fail on precision only). All three runs found the same five matters through file-name searches and scans and read their financing documents. They split at screening: T0 and T2 read the asset-purchase agreement, engagement letter (and in T2 the diligence memo and closing checklist) of a sale-side buyer matter and then wrote it into the answer, T0 as relevant on a broad reading and T2 as actual involvement. T1 listed that matter's files but never opened its documents and left it out. The critic's reviews did not differ in a way that explains the split: in T0 the write review asked whether the peripheral matter belonged and in T2 the screening review called its role thinly evidenced, but in both runs later check reviews said not to change the matter set.
